clue.text: Springtime in Kirkwall and one goes between leaf on left and right

indicators.note: the single letter for 'one' is placed between the abbreviation for the left-hand leaf and the letter for right

parts.note: VO is the abbreviation of verso, the left-hand page of an open book
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A seasonal note from Orkney, apparently about a leaf placed between pages of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirkwall is the chief town of Orkney, where voar is the dialect word for spring. 'Goes between' puts A (one) between VO (verso, the left-hand page) and R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Voar is the Northern Isles dialect name for the spring season, so it is springtime as said in Kirkwall.

clue.text: Half-hearted subject, to do with the Tube

parts.note: a vassal is a subject owing service to a feudal lord

explanation.surface: A lukewarm subject to do with the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' halves the doubled SS at the heart of VASSAL. The Tube is not the London Underground but an anatomical vessel or duct, Latin vas.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasal is an anatomy adjective for a vas, a vessel or duct in the body.

clue.text: Dark blues, before taking degree, excel

parts.note: the Dark Blues are Oxford University's sporting teams, OU

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the word for before has the degree letter inside it

parts.note: to means before in telling the time, as in ten to six

explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass or beat others, which is what excelling over them means.

clue.text: What Shakespeare cried — 'Bizarre English!'

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried' looks like an exclamation, but it means the tears he shed: rume is Shakespeare's spelling of rheum.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum, spelt rume in old texts, is a Shakespearean word for tears, so it is what was wept.

clue.text: One who's this wasted tenner with it

definitions.text: One who's this wasted tenner with it

parts.note: an imp is a cheeky child

explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the answer itself, so 'one who's this' is an imp; 'wasted' turns TENNER and IT into ERTINENT. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means rude or cheeky, the very manner of a mischievous child who blows a tenner.

clue.text: One regurgitating penny lodged in cloaca

clue.text: Swag tax officer smuggled

explanation.definitionFit: A toran is a decorative hanging of leaves or flowers over an Indian doorway, a festoon.

clue.text: Cacophony gone, member of wind section not flat at fringes

explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an old word for noisy merriment or din, so it is an obsolete cacophony.

clue.text: Pest controller, chap introduced to new chart nervously

explanation.definitionFit: A wantcatcher is a molecatcher, hired to rid fields and lawns of moles.

clue.text: Centre-half chasing Scottish ball — Gareth ——?

clue.text: Maybe strip rifle in pieces, needing help all round

clue.text: Obscure eccentric, obtrusive pushing out rank

explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy means unclear or murky, which is what obscure means as an adjective.

clue.text: Before fully imbibing liquor, boil tea vigorously as old-style cordial (13, two words)

clue.text: As part of custom, periodically one dances to jazz

clue.text: Is past time with fuel squandered, disinclined to recycle?

clue.text: Type of atom, name associated with old geometrician, first to last

indicators.note: the first letter of the geometrician's name is moved to the end

parts.note: Euclid was the ancient Greek author of the Elements of geometry
